justification: Infra: deploy the NARCliM climate-projection rasters to the Python API/PDF runtime via an R2 startup-download, mirroring the existing Hawkesbury pattern. Changes the deployed image (Dockerfile.python) and makes climate_risk_raster.DATA_DIR env-configurable. Standard tier — no DB writes, no user-facing copy; the risk is the API failing to start or the reader looking in the wrong dir, both guarded (download exits 0 always, DATA_DIR default unchanged when NARCLIM_DIR unset).

pre_impl.existing_data: 6 NARCliM 2.0 NetCDFs (~1.8 GB) found in Downloads and validated via query_narclim_summary (real Sydney projection: extreme-heat days 15.5 baseline -> 34.8 late-century high). R2 access confirmed (bucket nsw-planning-pdfs); narclim/ prefix was empty and is now populated by the upload. Hawkesbury rasters already deploy via the same R2 startup-download pattern.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: climate_risk_raster.DATA_DIR was a FIXED repo path (data/narclim), not writable/relocatable on Railway. Made it read NARCLIM_DIR (default unchanged for local dev). The Python API + conveyancing PDF share Dockerfile.python, whose CMD chains raster downloads before uvicorn — so one startup-download line unblocks both the climate product and the (future) PDF section.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: prior-art audited 2026-07-07: download_narclim_rasters.py mirrors download_hawkesbury_rasters.py (same R2 client, head-then-skip, exit-0 contract); no new hazard logic. climate_risk_raster reader reused unchanged except the env-aware DATA_DIR.

functions.name: main
functions.input: R2 env vars (account/key/secret/bucket) and NARCLIM_DIR; no arguments
functions.output: downloads the 6 NARCliM .nc files from r2://<bucket>/narclim/ to NARCLIM_DIR, skipping files already present at the correct size
functions.if_none: missing R2 env vars or boto3 -> logs a warning and returns (exit 0); a per-file download failure is logged, the partial file removed, and the run continues — never crashes the container startup

values.value: the raster directory (NARCLIM_DIR) that both the download destination and the reader resolve to
values.nullable: yes — env var may be unset
values.if_missing: reader defaults to repo/data/narclim (unchanged local-dev behaviour); download script defaults to /tmp/narclim (writable on Railway). Dockerfile.python sets NARCLIM_DIR=/tmp/narclim so both agree in the deployed image
values.guard_at: tests assert both honour NARCLIM_DIR and the download default is a /tmp path (never a possibly-read-only repo path)

queries: N/A — no database access; this is deploy wiring plus an object-store fetch.

break_it.scenario: R2 is unreachable or creds missing at container startup
break_it.what_happens: the download script logs a warning and exits 0; uvicorn still starts; climate_risk_score/query_narclim catch FileNotFoundError and drop the projection component — the API serves, the projections show their existing honest gap
break_it.how: all([R2 env]) guard + try/except around boto3 and each download; CMD uses && but the script always exits 0
break_it.repro: unset R2 env and run: python scripts/download_narclim_rasters.py (exits 0, warns)

break_it.scenario: Someone adds a scenario to climate_risk_raster.NARCLIM_FILES but not to the download list
break_it.what_happens: the new scenario would query a file the deploy never downloads -> a silent projection gap in prod
break_it.how: test_download_list_matches_raster_manifest asserts the two lists are identical set-equal

break_it.scenario: NARCLIM_DIR points the reader somewhere the download script did not write
break_it.what_happens: reader FileNotFoundError -> projection gap, not a crash; but the two would silently disagree
break_it.how: both DEST_DIR and DATA_DIR read the SAME NARCLIM_DIR var; tests assert each honours it; Dockerfile sets one value for both

post_merge.secrets: No new secrets — the R2 creds (R2_ACCOUNT_ID/ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/BUCKET_NAME) are already on the Python service for the Hawkesbury download. NARCLIM_DIR is baked into Dockerfile.python. Confirm the R2 creds are present on the service post-deploy.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes — after Railway rebuilds Dockerfile.python, check the deploy logs for '[narclim-dl] 6/6 raster files ready in /tmp/narclim', then hit POST /pipeline/climate-risk (or run a conveyancing report) at a Sydney address and confirm the NARCliM heat/projection component is now populated rather than showing the honest gap.
